name: Abbie's World motif, aesthetic and palette rubric
source_enum_note: source values are the identity schema's enum (docs/oracle/identity/game-identity.schema.json): footage_cv = computer vision over our own captures, llm_judge = VLM with saved prompt, pairwise and both orders, playtrace = in-game log, human = Evan or a child playtest, estimate = not yet measured.
colour_space: OKLab / OKLCH (Ottosson 2020). CVD simulation: Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes 2009 at severity 1.0.

layers.motif: a recurring shape, object or pattern that carries the world's identity and usually a meaning (the bell, the teal roof cap)
layers.shape_language: which primitive (round, square, triangle) each family of things is built from, and what that says (round = friendly, square = steady, triangle = alert)
layers.aesthetic: the whole set of choices (rendering, material, proportion, detail density, motion, light) that makes every asset look like it came from one hand
layers.palette: the structured set of colours: roles, value plan, hue families, saturation ladder, accent budget, and how it shifts with time, season, weather and mood

information_modes.diegetic: the world's own colour changes (crop wilts to straw, windows glow at dusk)
information_modes.spatial: colour on a cue attached to a thing, presentation layer only (need bubble)
information_modes.meta: a grade on the lens for a feeling (gentle warm vignette at bedtime)
information_modes.overlay: a precise colour key on screen (the hand of cards' suit colours)
information_modes.none: the world's palette just shifts and the child feels it (autumn)

targets_doc.value_bands: OKLab L thresholds for dark | mid | light bands (notan)
targets_doc.band_floor: a band counts when it holds at least this share of world pixels
targets_doc.figure_ground_dL: minimum OKLab L difference between every figure role and every ground role
targets_doc.cvd_min_de: minimum OKLab distance between a meaning and its ground (and meanings sharing a ground) in normal vision and under protan, deutan and tritan simulation
targets_doc.night_dL_min: world mean lightness must fall at least this much from day to night
targets_doc.accent_share_max: share of pixels that are accents (chroma >= accent_chroma and >= 2x median)
targets_doc.world_chroma: band for mean world chroma (OKLCH): below is muddy, above is neon
targets_doc.in_gamut_min: share of world pixels within in_gamut_de of a declared palette role
targets_doc.ui_from_world_de: every UI colour (except ink) within this distance of a world role

gates.check: The world reads in greyscale: every capture has at least two value bands over the floor and RMS lightness contrast over the minimum, and every figure role separates from every ground role in lightness.
Every state shown by colour also shows by shape, motion or sound.
Every meaning separates from its ground, and from meanings that share that ground, under normal vision and protan, deutan and tritan simulation.

Each signal (time, season, weather, mood) drives at least three world channels, and its states really differ in the world: night is darker than day by the minimum; other states differ by palette distance or warmth. A change that only re-tints the UI fails.
gates.method: captures per state, or specified sky colours until captured

gates.check: No axis primaries (#ff0000, #00ff00, #0000ff) or missing-texture magenta in the world over 0.1% of pixels.
No alarm red for failure, no flashing over 3 Hz, no draining of colour as a punishment.
Nothing copies a studied game's expression: its particular palette as a whole, character designs, motifs, textures, logos. Style (principles, structures, ratios) is free.
gates.method: aesthetic-signatures.json classes; llm_judge pairwise against reference games

checks.check: At least 3 motifs, each appearing in 3 or more things.
At least 3 families of things declare a primitive, using at least 2 different primitives.
At 48 px, blurred and greyscale, a VLM (later a child) names home, barn, animal and tree from silhouettes alone; score = correct / shown.
Each motif means something in play (brass means 'something to know'; the teal cap means 'a home for someone').
At least 80% of world pixels sit near a declared palette role.
Shown an asset beside the world, pairwise and both orders, a VLM says it belongs; at least 90% of assets.
Edge treatment, detail density and material roles are the same across assets (identity schema assets.geometry and assets.materials).
Each place speaks the shared grammar in its own materials (Ranch: wood, bells, painted signs; Moonbase: lights, radio, holograms).
5 to 12 roles in at most 6 hue families.
Accents cover at most 12% of the world.
Figures are more saturated than the ground they stand on, and the backdrop is the quietest.
The key light is warm and shadows lean cool (or the reverse at night), never grey.
World mean chroma sits in the band: rich, not muddy, not neon.
At least 3 states are shown by the world's own colour (diegetic), not by a UI badge.
No colour means two things.
Signal hues (brass, lamp glow, storm slate) appear only where they mean their thing.
Every meaning differs from its ground in lightness too.
At least 4 times of day (dawn, day, dusk, night) with their own sky and sun.
At least 3 seasons with captures.
A colour script: each story beat or mood has a palette, and the music bible's mood for that beat agrees.
Worst CVD distance is at least 1.25x the gate minimum.
No large pure-white or pure-black fields (sky and panels stay inside L 0.12 to 0.96).
Every UI colour comes from the world palette; no web blues.
No neutral grey fills in the UI; glass takes the world's warmth.
The liquid glass has depth (rim light, refraction of the world behind it, a shadow on the world), not a flat frosted panel.
Pickers show live previews in the world's palette, not icons.

core_rule.text: One game-state signal moves the whole palette together: sky, sun, fog, windows, foliage, water, music and sound. Colour is a channel of the whole-game adaptation from the HUD study, never a separate theme switch for the UI.

keep: liquid glass as objects with depth
lose: web-page palette: grey panels, system blue, white cards
flat colour themes that re-skin the UI but leave the world unchanged
